issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature includes a second boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)), while the problem statement (and the UML/tasks) require addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. The solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with one parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about which signature to implement and may cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java. If input validation is desired as a teaching point, either implement it inside that single-parameter method or provide an overloaded private helper method, but keep the public API matching the problem statement.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), but the problem statement and the solution implementation specify addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in method signature for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) creates confusion for students about the expected API and will cause compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } If input validation is desired, implement it internally or provide an overloaded private helper rather than exposing a boolean parameter that the problem does not mention.
